README.md

README on GitHub ↗

Saved keyboard lighting for your Redragon K686 MAX on Linux.

Download · Installation · Features · Getting started · Advanced guide

Redragon Control is a Linux desktop app for the Redragon K686WBG-RGB-MAX. Choose lighting that stays saved on your keyboard and keep your favorite setups in reusable profiles. Keyboard access is limited to explicit lighting changes. Closing the window quits the app; there is no tray or login startup.

Before you download: other Redragon models are not currently supported. Lighting changes require the 2.4 GHz USB receiver. See connection support for details.

What changed in 0.2.7

The app now controls onboard lighting only. Live key/wheel remapping, input observation, the tray indicator, login startup, and background reconnect/retry have been removed. Continuous input interception could cause missed or repeated keystrokes; the wheel and keys now keep their normal hardware behavior.

Open the app, choose your lighting, select Save to keyboard, then close the window. The keyboard connection closes after each lighting transaction, and closing the last window exits the app. Lighting continues on the keyboard. Opening the updated app also disables this app’s old startup entries and stops legacy background workers. Older profiles remain readable, but their key bindings are never activated.

See the 0.2.7 release notes for fixes and validation.

Features

Feature What you can do
Saved keyboard lighting Choose seven static colors, adjust brightness, or turn the lights off. Your lighting stays on the keyboard after you quit the app.
17 built-in animations Pick effects such as Rainbow, Smooth breathing, Raindrops, and typing-reactive lighting. Adjust brightness and animation speed in five levels.
Profiles Save named setups, switch between them, and import or export lighting preferences as a file.
Desktop appearance Use Adwaita or match your Omarchy desktop palette. Automatic mode chooses the appropriate appearance for your desktop.
Recovery tools Restore backed-up keyboard lighting, reset the app's settings, or follow the keyboard factory-reset instructions.
Demo mode and command line Explore the interface without changing a keyboard, or use command-line tools for setup, profiles, diagnostics, and automation.

The app uses native GTK 4 and libadwaita. It includes no telemetry or firmware flashing tools. Command-line options are covered in the advanced guide.

Installation

We recommend Gear Lever for easy installation, an app-menu shortcut, and updates in one place. It manages the AppImage for you without terminal commands.

1. Download the AppImage

Open the latest release and download the file ending in x86_64.AppImage under Assets. The AppImage is the application; the .zsync and .sha256 files are used for updates and download verification.

You need a 64-bit x86 Linux desktop. The AppImage includes the app's Python, GTK, and other application libraries, so you do not need to install them separately.

2. Add it to Gear Lever (recommended)

  1. Install Gear Lever from Flathub if you do not already have it.
  2. Open Gear Lever and drag the downloaded AppImage into its window. Follow its prompts to add the app to your application menu.
  3. Launch Redragon Control from your application menu to begin setup.

Gear Lever can discover the update source included in the AppImage and offer new stable versions. You control when it checks for updates and installs them; see Startup and updates.

Advanced users: run the AppImage manually

If you prefer to manage the file yourself, keep it in a permanent location, such as an Applications folder in your home directory. In your file manager, open its Properties, allow it to run as a program, then double-click it. The exact wording depends on your desktop.

Alternatively, run these commands from the folder containing your download (replace VERSION with the version in its filename):

chmod +x Redragon-Control-VERSION-x86_64.AppImage
./Redragon-Control-VERSION-x86_64.AppImage

Keep the file in a convenient location. To update manually, close the app before replacing the image, then launch the new version.

3. Enable keyboard access

On the first setup screen, select Enable keyboard access and approve your desktop's administrator prompt. This gives the app access to the keyboard’s lighting settings. The app itself runs as your normal user. Reconnect the keyboard or receiver if prompted.

Your desktop needs Polkit and a working authentication agent to show this prompt. No separate setup script download is required for the AppImage. Virtual input and input-event permissions are no longer installed.

Coming from Flatpak? Export your profiles, quit the old app's keyboard services, then import the profiles in the AppImage. See the migration guide.

Getting started

  1. Connect your keyboard. Plug in the receiver and switch the keyboard to 2.4G.
  2. Follow the setup screens. Select your keyboard and enable access if needed. You can choose lighting or import a profile. Apply saves and activates your changes; Next continues without applying unsaved edits.
  3. Open the app. Select Open Redragon Control at the end of setup. You can change your choices at any time using the steps below.

Set your lighting

Open Lighting, choose an effect, adjust the available settings, and select Save to keyboard. Make sure the 2.4 GHz receiver is selected.

  • Static color: choose red, green, blue, yellow, magenta, cyan, or white.
  • Smooth breathing: use one of the same seven colors with a gentle fade.
  • Other animations: choose a built-in pattern with its own onboard colors. Reactive effects respond when you type.
  • Off: turn the keyboard lighting off.

Lighting runs on the keyboard itself. You can close or quit the app after saving; no background lighting service is needed. The preview illustrates each effect, so colors and timing may differ from the physical keyboard.

See all 17 animation effects

Smooth breathing · Rainbow · Flash Away · Raindrops · Rainbow Wheel · Ripple Shining · Stars Twinkle · Shadow Disappear · Retro Snake · Neon Stream · Reaction · Sine Wave · Retinue Scanning · Rotating Windmill · Colorful Waterfall · Blossoming · Rotating Storm

Save and share profiles

Open the app menu to Save Named Profile, Load Named Profile, Import Profile, or Export Profile. Profiles contain your lighting preferences, making it easy to keep separate work and gaming setups or move them to another installation.

Loading or importing a profile updates the saved preferences. To send its lighting to the keyboard, select Save to keyboard. Legacy bindings in older profiles are retained for compatibility but are never activated.

Choose your appearance

Open Menu → Appearance and choose Automatic, Adwaita, or Omarchy. Automatic follows the current Omarchy palette on Omarchy and uses Adwaita on other desktops. Appearance is saved separately from your keyboard profiles.

Supported connections

Support is specific to the Redragon K686WBG-RGB-MAX. Similar model names or shared USB identifiers do not guarantee compatibility.

Feature USB cable 2.4 GHz receiver Bluetooth
Save static color, brightness, or lights off Not supported Supported Not supported
Save built-in lighting animations Not supported Supported — 17 effects Not supported

USB lighting writes are disabled because a reliable way to save lighting over the cable has not been verified. Use the receiver for all lighting changes. The wheel and keys keep their normal hardware behavior. Custom remapping has been removed because it requires continuous input interception and can cause missed or repeated keystrokes.

Startup and updates

The app opens only when launched manually. Closing its window quits it. It creates no indicator and never restores services at login or reconnect. Opening this version disables this app’s legacy login entry, removes its managed Omarchy startup hook, and stops old tray and keyboard workers. Demo mode leaves saved settings alone; custom --config launches stop workers only for that configuration and leave the normal login entry alone.

Gear Lever is the recommended way to manage updates. Open it to check for new versions of Redragon Control. AppImage builds include an update source that Gear Lever can discover and use to offer stable releases, without requiring you to enter an update URL. You control update checking and installation in Gear Lever. Older images without this metadata need one manual update or a one-time update-source configuration. See the Gear Lever update guide.

Close the app before replacing the AppImage, then open the updated image. When upgrading from an older tray-based release, use its Quit and stop keyboard services menu item before replacing it.

Troubleshooting and recovery

Problem or task What to do
Keyboard not detected Check the cable or receiver and mode switch, reconnect, then retry detection. Use Enable keyboard access if the setup screen reports missing permissions.
Lighting controls unavailable Select the receiver and switch to 2.4G. Lighting changes are unavailable over USB cable and Bluetooth.
AppImage reports a FUSE error Run ./Redragon-Control-VERSION-x86_64.AppImage --appimage-extract-and-run, replacing VERSION with your download's version.
Restore the original lighting Select the receiver and choose Restore previous lighting. This restores the configuration backed up before the app's first lighting save.
Reset app preferences Open Recovery → Reset app settings. This stops services and clears local lighting preferences and bindings. Named profiles and lighting already saved on the keyboard are kept.
Factory-reset the keyboard Close the app, then hold Fn + Esc for 3 seconds. The Recovery page also provides guidance.

If an older release leaves input unusable, quit its tray and unplug/reconnect the keyboard. This version removes input interception entirely. For further help, read the advanced guide or report an issue.

Report an issue

Found a bug or need help with something that is not covered above? You can report it on GitHub. You will need a free GitHub account to submit an issue.

  1. Check the existing issues to see whether someone has already reported the same problem. If so, add any useful details to that issue.
  2. Open a new issue.
  3. Give it a clear title, such as “Lighting cannot be saved through the receiver.”
  4. Describe the problem using the checklist below, then submit your issue.

Include as much of this information as you can:

  • App version: the version in your AppImage filename, and whether you use Gear Lever, run the AppImage manually, or run from source.
  • Linux setup: your distribution and desktop, such as Fedora with GNOME, KDE Plasma, or Omarchy.
  • Keyboard and connection: the exact keyboard model and whether you are using the USB cable, 2.4 GHz receiver, or Bluetooth.
  • Steps to reproduce: what you clicked or changed before the problem appeared, and whether it happens every time.
  • Expected and actual behavior: what you wanted to happen and what happened instead.
  • Supporting details: the exact error message and any relevant screenshots or logs, if available. Remove personal information before sharing them.

You do not need to understand the app's code to report a problem. A clear example of what happened is a helpful starting point.
